text: Make the graph’s nodes shrink slightly when idle, then return to normal size. This draws attention to the graph’s activity without overwhelming the user, balancing visibility and calm. The trade-off is reduced precision in node size for better perceived liveliness.

name: Pane
text: The shrinking nodes risk training users to ignore the signal entirely—like a car alarm that blares until ignored. name: Pane
text: Edge pulses risk training users to treat every highlight as noise—like a stock ticker that blinks so often it’s ignored. A better alternative: fade the edge to a subtle, persistent color shift (e.g., a soft glow) for 3 seconds after new data arrives. Settle it by tracking how many users click on edges within 5 seconds of the change—fewer clicks mean the signal is too weak.
